Meeting header: 2025-04-29 16:00 UTC | Duration 55m | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Jared Lewis (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Yeo (Redwood SE), Elena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Diane Park (Blueforge Procurement), Owen Castillo (Blueforge Security), Maya Reynolds (Blueforge Legal), Kenji Ito (Blueforge Platform), Anita Gomez (Blueforge Finance)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): procurement kickoff to align MSA/DPA, SLA, pricing gate. Technical constraints around KMS and private deployment discussed. Action items assigned.

[00:00:00] Jared (AE): All right welcome everybody, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call — and then we'll jump into agenda. Appreciate you making time.
[00:00:12] Diane (Procurement): Hi, Diane here. Thanks Jared.
[00:00:15] Maya (Legal): Maya — hi all.
[00:00:17] Owen (Security): Owen on the call.
[00:00:19] Kenji: Kenji here.
[00:00:21] Anita: Anita, finance.
[00:00:23] Priya (SE): Priya from Redwood. Marcus and Elena are on as well.
[00:00:28] Jared: Cool. Quick run of agenda: MSA/DPA expectations, SLA and SLO targets, KMS/SSO and data residency, pricing pathway for pilot, and then technical on-boarding checklist. Any additions?
[00:00:40] Diana (sic) — note: speaker ID mis-labeled as Diana for Diane in transcript
[00:00:43] Diane: No, that looks good. We'll want to confirm auditing and retention too, sorry that's big for us.
[00:00:48] Jared: Yeah, we'll cover audit logs and retention windows.
[00:00:52] 
[00:00:55] Topic: MSA and DPA redlines
[00:00:56] Maya (Legal): To start, our legal team needs clarity on data processing obligations in the DPA — specifically subprocessor lists, cross-border transfer mechanics, and our ability to terminate if there's an incident. We also have questions on liability caps and indemnity in the MSA. We typically push for mutual indemnity but understand some vendors have carve-outs.
[00:01:18] Jared: Understood. We do provide a standard MSA and DPA — happy to send the redline-ready excerpt. For indemnity we have a few options depending on enterprise+ — we can show language that narrows IP indemnity and we can propose a higher cap for catastrophic security incidents.
[00:01:34] Maya: That would help. Also, we need to confirm if Redwood will sign a DPA with data residency restrictions — we will be hosting EU customer data only in eu-west for the pilot. Is that supported in hosted mode or do we need a dedicated zone?
[00:01:47] Priya: Short answer: yes, we have region pinning for hosted. For stricter guarantees we can do a private deployment/VPC on prem or dedicated capacity. For the hosted EU region we can route model inference and store short-lived artifacts in eu-west. For long-term retention or logs we can offer options — but we'll need to confirm retention window and whether logs leave region.
[00:02:10] Owen: That's key. We can't have logs exported to US without justification and legal controls. Also KMS — we require customer-managed keys for the pilot. Is BYOK supported?
[00:02:21] Marcus (SE): We support both BYOK and Redwood-managed KMS. BYOK requires a small onboarding step and we have an HSM integration; if you require HSM-backed keys we can accommodate with our private plane (sic) — private control plane — sorry. There may be minimal latency tradeoffs.
[00:02:36] Kenji: And for DB backups — are those encrypted with the same KMS? We have to map to our encryption policy.
[00:02:43] Priya: Yes backups and persistent logs can be encrypted with the customer-provided KMS when in dedicated or private. Hosted with BYOK is more nuanced — we can encrypt but some metadata may still be in Redwood control plane; we'll call that out in the DPA.
[00:02:58] 
[00:03:00] Topic: SLA / performance targets
[00:03:01] Diane: For accepted vendors we need a 99.9 uptime SLA for the inference endpoint and P99 token latency under 600ms for our median 1.5k prompt loads. How realistic is that?
[00:03:12] Priya: 99.9 uptime for the inference API is in line with our Dedicated offering. For P99 latency 600ms depends on model size and batch behavior. If you're using a large base model and long context, that will blow past 600ms. For a quantized medium model and dedicated GPUs we can hit sub-600ms for 1.5k token workloads in continuous batching, but it's workload-dependent. We'll run a benchmark to confirm.
[00:03:36] Kenji: We're expecting bursts during business hours — do you have autoscale and burst guarantees?
[00:03:40] Marcus: Yes autoscaling with reserved baseline and burst capacity. The burst is best-effort above committed capacity; for contractual SLAs we typically define committed throughput and then provide best-effort burst. For hard guarantees you'd lock additional reserved capacity.
[00:03:53] Anita: Pricing question — if we need guaranteed throughput, how does that move pricing? We need a rough delta to get budget approval.
[00:03:59] Jared: We'll share a pilot pricing sheet that shows hosted usage vs dedicated reserved monthly commit, with delta for reserved capacity and the expected unit cost per token. We'll also show an escrowing/overage approach.
[00:04:10] 
[00:04:12] Topic: Security posture and audits
[00:04:13] Owen: SOC2 is table stakes — do you have scope documentation and last audit date? Also we'd like pen test reports and the ability to add Blueforge to the subprocessor list notification.
[00:04:24] Elena (CSM): We are SOC2 Type II certified — last audit report is Q1 2025. Pen test summary and redacted report can be shared under NDA. For subprocessor notifications we have a portal and 30-day notice for major changes.
[00:04:37] Owen: Cool. Also, RBAC and SSO — SAML/OIDC? And can we map roles to our internal groups?
[00:04:43] Priya: We support SAML SSO and OIDC. RBAC supports custom roles and SCIM provisioning if you want automated mapping.
[00:04:50] Maya: On auditability — log retention is important. We need 12 months of detailed audit logs accessible for export with an immutable retention flag. Is that possible?
[00:04:58] Marcus: For dedicated/private we can meet a 12-month retention and can provide log export endpoints. For hosted we have configurable retention up to 90 days by default and extended retention as an add-on — which could get to 12 months if contracted.
[00:05:12] 
[00:05:15] Topic: Procurement path and approvals
[00:05:16] Diane: Blueforge procurement needs a pricing gate: pilot cost estimate, then a finance sign-off. What's the fastest route to get pricing approved internally?
[00:05:24] Jared: We'll provide a clear pilot pricing sheet (line items for compute, storage, data transfer, KMS licensing). We'll also include a model of cost per million tokens at expected QPS so your finance team can model monthly spend.
[00:05:36] Anita: Is there a contractual minimum commitment for the pilot? We prefer month-to-month for pilot but some vendors insist on quarterly minimums.
[00:05:42] Jared: For pilots we typically do month-to-month with an agreed committed baseline you'd pay for if you exceed, or we can do a short-term reserved pool for predictable pricing. We'll document both options.
[00:05:52] 
[00:05:55] Topic: Technical onboarding checklist (high level)
[00:05:56] Priya: High-level checklist we'll follow: network egress/IP allowlist, SAML SSO setup, KMS BYOK handshake, test dataset upload schema, benchmark test harness, cost telemetry hooks, and rollback/fallback policy. We'll send a one-page checklist after the call.
[00:06:10] Kenji: For network egress, we need an IP allowlist and also to control egress to third-party telemetry. Also we need to keep the KV cache strictly in-region.
[00:06:18] Marcus: We'll share the IP blocks and have an option for private peering for dedicated deployments. Regarding KV cache — yes we can keep it in-region for dedicated/private; hosted may have small control-plane metadata outside region but we will state that in the DPA.
[00:06:33] 
[00:06:36] Topic: Benchmarks and acceptance tests
[00:06:37] Priya: We'll run benchmarks simulating 1.5k token prompts at your expected QPS. For acceptance we recommend: 1) P99 latency threshold, 2) throughput target, 3) no data egress exceptions, 4) KMS wrap validation, 5) logging/retention verification.
[00:06:52] Maya: We'll need to see raw logs from the benchmark and cost estimate to validate.
[00:06:55] Priya: We'll provide a zipped archive of benchmark logs and a spreadsheet mapping cost per run. Link will be posted to the shared drive.
[00:07:02] 
[00:07:05] CROSSTALK / minor interruptions
[00:07:06] Anita: Sorry, one more finance check — if we execute BYOK, does that change the monthly fee?
[00:07:10] Jared: Minor fee for HSM-backed BYOK in private plane — there is a small licensing add-on. We'll include both in the pricing sheet.
[00:07:18] 
[00:07:20] Topic: Legal specifics and redline process
[00:07:21] Maya: Our legal team will send an exception list with the top items: cap on liability, subprocessor flow-down obligations, data residency clause, right to audit, and indemnity carveouts. We expect Redwood to propose counter language for the first pass.
[00:07:38] Jared: Agreed. We'll return an MSA draft with comments ready for Maya by 2025-05-02. We'll also call out the DPA appendix that covers EU-only processing and BYOK implications.
[00:07:50] Maya: Also please include sample confidentiality language that covers model artifacts — we treat model outputs derived from our private data as potentially sensitive.
[00:07:58] Priya: We'll flag model output handling in the DPA and the onboarding checklist. For private deployments the artifacts live in your VPC and we can set stricter retention and output routing.
[00:08:10] 
[00:08:12] Topic: Risk & mitigations
[00:08:13] Owen: Primary risk is inadvertent cross-region log transfer and key management handoff. Mitigation: prove BYOK and in-region retention in an initial bench.
[00:08:22] Marcus: We'll script tests that demonstrate no logs leave eu-west and produce signed attestations. There's a small chance of metadata in the control plane leaving region depending on service mode, we'll document that.
[00:08:34] 
[00:08:36] Mid-call status check (approx 45m remaining)
[00:08:38] Jared: Quick check — are we comfortable with the org-level asks and timelines?
[00:08:42] Diane: Yes, main blockers are the legal exceptions and finance pilot approvals.
[00:08:46] Anita: Ok.

[00:08:50] Topic: Pricing approval pathway details
[00:08:51] Anita: For an internal fast-track we need a single-line item with total expected monthly and a notes sheet. Can Redwood produce a short one-pager for finance?
[00:08:59] Jared: Absolutely — one-pager with monthly expected, high, mid, low scenarios, and committed vs burst cost. We'll send to Anita and Diane.
[00:09:06] Anita: Also include data transfer estimate for EU egress — our CFO flags cross-border egress fees heavily.
[00:09:12] Priya: We'll include expected egress numbers with the pilot's expected QPS; and an optional private peering cost to avoid public egress charges.
[00:09:20]

[00:09:23] Jared: Proposed timeline: Week 1 — legal exceptions list & Redwood MSA draft; Week 2 — bench run and KMS handshake; Week 3 — pilot kickoff; Week 4-6 — pilot evaluation and SLA acceptance tests. Does that align with your internal gates?
